Capacitor in an AC circuit: the current phasor leads the voltage phasor by 90 degrees

Animation. On the left, two phasors rotate counter-clockwise about the origin: the voltage phasor V0 in blue and the current phasor I0 in red, half as long and a quarter turn ahead of it, their labels turning with them; a small arc marks the 90 degree lead. On the right, their projections on the y axis, v_C(t) in blue and i_C(t) in red, are traced out against time: the current is a cosine, peaking a quarter period before the voltage. A small schematic shows an AC source driving a capacitor.
